chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: I heard him say,
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “I do not carry out amputation for open snatching, which is al-khulsah, but I do administer ta'zir upon him.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, the source of the ruling
key_terms.أُعَزِّرُهُ: I administer discretionary punishment to him
key_terms.الزَّعَارَةِ الْمُعْلَنَةِ: openly committed theft or public snatching
key_terms.الْخُلْسَةُ: snatching or seizing property quickly and openly
key_terms.لَا أَقْطَعُ: I do not apply the punishment of amputation

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd of amputation applied for open snatching theft in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding openly committed snatching theft. It states that the hadd punishment of amputation is not applied in such a case, but the offender is instead subject to ta'zir.
